title: You can give, or take
hook: Does adding a take option change what a donation means?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Inspect how the feasible choice set changes the interpretation of zero giving.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Inspect how the feasible choice set changes the interpretation of zero giving.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: A toy giver can transfer any integer from 0 to 5. If taking is added, transfers −5 through 5 become possible. How many distinct transfers are now feasible? Toy inputs A=[-5, 5]; B=[0, 5].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[11, -5, 5], [6, 0, 5]]. Labels: Feasible integers, Minimum, Maximum.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: Adding negative transfers changes what zero means within the feasible set. The comparison widens the set from giving-only to taking-or-giving. This exposes a design difference without predicting what any participant will choose.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Minimum transfer=0, Maximum transfer=5. What is Feasible integers? Answer: 6.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Minimum transfer=0, Maximum transfer=5. What is Feasible integers?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 6. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: Adding an option to take money from the recipient sharply cuts giving (List, 2007; Bardsley, 2008).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Inspect how the feasible choice set changes the interpretation of zero giving.
